templates.title: Height of a building from two angles of elevation

variants.problem: From a point on level ground, the angle of elevation to the top of a cliff is $38^\circ$. After walking $100$ ft directly away from it, the angle of elevation is $25^\circ$. How tall is the cliff?
variants.solution:
Let $h$ be the height and $d$ the first distance. Two right triangles give

\[h=d\tan38^\circ\qquad\text{and}\qquad h=(d+100)\tan25^\circ.\]

Set them equal: $d(\tan38^\circ-\tan25^\circ)=100\tan25^\circ$, so

\[d=\frac{100\tan25^\circ}{\tan38^\circ-\tan25^\circ}\approx148.04\ \text{ft},\qquad h=d\tan38^\circ\approx115.7\ \text{ft}.\]

templates.title: Area swept by a windshield wiper

variants.problem: A wiper blade $16$ inches long is mounted on a $22$-inch arm, so the blade runs from $6$ to $22$ inches from the pivot. The wiper turns through $105^\circ$. How much area does the blade sweep clean?
variants.solution:

templates.title: Linked sprockets: how fast does the bike go?

variants.problem: A cyclist pedals at $60$ revolutions per minute. The front sprocket has radius $6$ in and the rear sprocket has radius $2.5$ in; the rear wheel (radius $14$ in) turns with the rear sprocket. How fast is the bicycle moving, in miles per hour? (1 mile = 63,360 in.)
variants.solution:
The chain moves at the same linear speed around both sprockets. Front sprocket: $60$ rev/min $=120\pi$ rad/min, so the chain speed is

\[v=6\cdot120\pi=720\pi\approx2261.9\ \text{in/min}.\]

Rear sprocket angular speed: $\omega=\frac{v}{2.5}\approx904.8$ rad/min. The wheel turns at the same $\omega$, so its rim moves at

\[14\omega\approx12,666.9\ \text{in/min}=\frac{12,666.9\cdot60}{63{,}360}\approx12.00\ \text{mph}.\]

The chain moves at the same linear speed around both sprockets. Front sprocket: $90$ rev/min $=180\pi$ rad/min, so the chain speed is

\[v=8\cdot180\pi=1440\pi\approx4523.9\ \text{in/min}.\]

Rear sprocket angular speed: $\omega=\frac{v}{2.5}\approx1809.6$ rad/min. The wheel turns at the same $\omega$, so its rim moves at

\[14\omega\approx25,333.8\ \text{in/min}=\frac{25,333.8\cdot60}{63{,}360}\approx23.99\ \text{mph}.\]

variants.problem: A circular pond of radius $25$ m is centered at the origin. A straight path runs from $(33,-6)$ to $(6,33)$. At which two points does the path cross the edge of the pond?

whose roots are $x=24$ and $x=15$.

The path crosses the edge at $(24,7)$ and $(15,20)$.

variants.solution:
In $32$ s the runner covers $5\cdot32=160$ m of arc, which is an angle of $\frac{160}{60}=2.6667$ rad.

The start is at angle $0$ (measured counterclockwise from east), so the runner is now at angle $\theta=0-2.6667\approx-2.6667$ rad:

\[(x,y)=\left(60\cos\theta,\ 60\sin\theta\right)\approx(-53.36,\ -27.44).\]

$f(g(x))=(2 x + 2)+3\left|2 x\right|$. The absolute value switches where $2 x=0$, at $x=0$.

\[f(g(x))=\begin{cases}8 x + 2, & x\ge 0\\ 2 - 4 x, & x< 0\end{cases}\]

Solve $14$ on each piece and keep only solutions in that piece's range:

  • $8 x + 2=14$ gives $x=\frac{3}{2}$ (valid).
  • $2 - 4 x=14$ gives $x=-3$ (valid).

Solutions: $x=-3$, $x=\frac{3}{2}$.

templates.title: When will two exponentially growing towns be the same size?

variants.problem: Arden has $1,325$ people and grows by $8\%$ per year. Brookfield has $30,000$ people and its population doubles every $40$ years. After how many years will the two towns have the same population?
variants.solution:
With $t$ in years: $A(t)=1,325(1+0.08)^t$ and $B(t)=30,000\cdot2^{t/40}$. Set them equal and take logarithms:

\[\ln 1325+t\ln(1.08)=\ln 30000+\frac{t}{40}\ln2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad t=\frac{\ln(30000/1325)}{\ln(1.08)-\frac{\ln2}{40}}\approx52.32\ \text{years}.\]

variants.problem:
Let $f(x)=ax-2$ and suppose $f(f(x))=9 x - 8$.

(a) Find $a$.
(b) Find $f^{-1}(x)$.
variants.solution:
(a) $f(f(x))=a\left(ax-2\right)-2=a^2x-2a-2$. Matching coefficients with $9 x - 8$:

\[a^2=9\qquad\text{and}\qquad -2a-2=-8.\]

The first gives $a=\pm3$; the second gives $a=\frac{-8-(-2)}{-2}=3$. So $a=3$.

(b) Solve $y=3x-2$ for $x$: $x=\frac{y+2}{3}$, so

\[f^{-1}(x)=\frac{x}{3} + \frac{2}{3}.\]

(a) Find $a$.
(b) Find $f^{-1}(x)$.
variants.solution:
(a) $f(f(x))=a\left(ax-6\right)-6=a^2x-6a-6$. Matching coefficients with $4 x - 18$:

\[a^2=4\qquad\text{and}\qquad -6a-6=-18.\]

The first gives $a=\pm2$; the second gives $a=\frac{-18-(-6)}{-6}=2$. So $a=2$.

(b) Solve $y=2x-6$ for $x$: $x=\frac{y+6}{2}$, so

\[f^{-1}(x)=\frac{x}{2} + 3.\]

\[a^2=16\qquad\text{and}\qquad 1a+1=-3.\]

The first gives $a=\pm4$; the second gives $a=\frac{-3-(1)}{1}=-4$. So $a=-4$.

(b) Solve $y=-4x+1$ for $x$: $x=\frac{y-1}{-4}$, so

\[f^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{4} - \frac{x}{4}.\]

templates.title: Two linear models: when are they equal?

variants.problem: The price of item A grows linearly: $8$ dollars in year $1$ and $14$ dollars in year $3$. Item B also changes linearly: $36$ dollars in year $0$ and $27$ dollars in year $6$. In what year are the prices equal, and what is the price then?
variants.solution:
A: slope $\frac{14-8}{3-1}=3$, so $P_A(t)=3 t + 5$. B: slope $\frac{27-36}{6-0}=- \frac{3}{2}$, so $P_B(t)=36 - \frac{3 t}{2}$.

\[3 t + 5=36 - \frac{3 t}{2}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad t=\frac{36-5}{3-\left(- \frac{3}{2}\right)}=\frac{62}{9}\approx6.89.\]

The common price is $P_A(\frac{62}{9})=\frac{77}{3}\approx25.67$ dollars.

A: slope $\frac{\frac{53}{4}-\frac{41}{4}}{7-3}=\frac{3}{4}$, so $P_A(t)=\frac{3 t}{4} + 8$. B: slope $\frac{25-26}{5-4}=-1$, so $P_B(t)=30 - t$.

\[\frac{3 t}{4} + 8=30 - t\quad\Longrightarrow\quad t=\frac{30-8}{\frac{3}{4}-\left(-1\right)}=\frac{88}{7}\approx12.57.\]

The common price is $P_A(\frac{88}{7})=\frac{122}{7}\approx17.43$ dollars.

A: slope $\frac{25-22}{3-2}=3$, so $P_A(t)=3 t + 16$. B: slope $\frac{\frac{19}{2}-11}{7-6}=- \frac{3}{2}$, so $P_B(t)=20 - \frac{3 t}{2}$.

\[3 t + 16=20 - \frac{3 t}{2}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad t=\frac{20-16}{3-\left(- \frac{3}{2}\right)}=\frac{8}{9}\approx0.89.\]

The common price is $P_A(\frac{8}{9})=\frac{56}{3}\approx18.67$ dollars.

templates.title: Cut a wire into a polygon and a circle to minimize total area

variants.problem: A wire $120$ cm long is cut into two pieces. One piece is bent into an equilateral triangle and the other into a circle. Where should the wire be cut to make the total enclosed area as small as possible? What is that area?
variants.answer: Equilateral triangle gets $\approx74.79$ cm; minimum area $\approx431.77$ cm²
variants.solution:
Let $x$ be the length used for the equilateral triangle, so its side is $\frac x3$ and its area ($\frac{\sqrt3}{4}$side$^2$) is $\frac{\sqrt3}{36}x^2$. The circle gets $120-x$, so its radius is $\frac{120-x}{2\pi}$. The total area is

\[A(x)=\frac{\sqrt3}{36}x^2+\pi\left(\frac{120-x}{2\pi}\right)^2=\frac{\sqrt3}{36}x^2+\frac{(120-x)^2}{4\pi},\]

a quadratic in $x$ that opens upward. Its vertex (where $A'(x)=0$) is at

\[x=\frac{120/(2\pi)}{2\left(0.048113+\frac1{4\pi}\right)}\approx74.79\ \text{cm}.\]

So use about $74.79$ cm for the equilateral triangle and $45.21$ cm for the circle. The minimum total area is $A\approx431.77$ cm².

templates.title: Two people walking in straight lines: when are they closest?

variants.problem:
At $t=0$ Ann starts at $(-10,7)$ and walks in a straight line at constant speed, reaching $(10,-3)$ at $t=8$ s. At the same moment Ben starts at $(4,-12)$ and walks straight to $(2,11)$, arriving at $t=8$ s. (Units: meters.)

When are they closest together (during the first $8$ s), and how close do they get?
variants.solution:
Ann: $x=-10+2.5t$, $y=7-1.25t$. Ben: $x=4-0.25t$, $y=-12+2.875t$.

The vector from Ben to Ann is $\langle -14+2.75t,\ 19-4.125t\rangle$, so the squared distance is

\[D(t)^2=(-14+2.75t)^2+(19-4.125t)^2=24.5781t^2-233.75t+557,\]

a quadratic opening upward. Its vertex is at $t=-\dfrac{-233.75}{2(24.5781)}\approx4.755$ s, which is within $[0,8]$. There

\[D=\sqrt{D(t)^2}\approx1.109\ \text{m}.\]

variants.problem:
A quantity is modeled by $H(x)=\dfrac{ax+b}{cx+1}$. It is $20$ at $x=0$, $30$ at $x=1$ and $\frac{100}{3}$ at $x=2$.

(a) Find $a$, $b$ and $c$.
(b) What value does $H$ approach in the long run?
variants.solution:
(a) $H(0)=b$, so $b=20$. Clear the denominator, $ax+b=H(x)(cx+1)$, at the other two points:

\[a + 20=30 c + 30,\qquad 2 a + 20=\frac{200 c}{3} + \frac{100}{3}.\]

Solving these two linear equations gives $a=40$ and $c=1$. So $H(x)=\dfrac{40 x + 20}{x + 1}$.

(b) For large $x$, $H(x)\approx\frac{ax}{cx}=\frac{a}{c}=40$.

variants.problem:
A quantity varies sinusoidally with time $t$ (hours). It reaches a maximum of $6$ at $t=3$ and the next minimum, $2$, at $t=8$.

(a) Find a formula $f(t)$.
(b) Find $f(10)$.
(c) After $t=3$, when does it first drop to $3.4$?
variants.solution:
(a) Half a period runs from the maximum to the minimum, so the period is $P=2(8-3)=10$. The midline is $\frac{6+(2)}{2}=4$ and the amplitude is $\frac{6-(2)}{2}=2$. A cosine starts at its maximum, so shift it to $t=3$:

\[f(t)=4+2\cos\!\left(\frac{2\pi}{10}(t-3)\right).\]

(b) $f(10)=4+2\cos\!\left(\frac{2\pi}{10}\cdot7\right)\approx3.38$.

(c) Solve $4+2\cos\!\left(\frac{2\pi}{10}(t-3)\right)=3.4$: $\cos(\cdot)=-0.3$. Going down from the maximum the angle increases from $0$, so the first solution is $\frac{2\pi}{10}(t-3)=\cos^{-1}(-0.3)\approx1.8755$:

\[t=3+\frac{10}{2\pi}\cos^{-1}(-0.3)\approx5.98.\]
